page: Amazon Web Services x1e.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Xen hypervisor, this server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 244.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 30.5 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the x1e.2xlarge exhibits limited computational and memory throughput performance relative to modern standards. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the bottom 10%, while multi-core CPU metrics and Passmark CPU scores reside in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes, consistently rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations such as Redis SET and static web serving throughput are positioned in the weak performance tier.

The primary tradeoff of the x1e.2xlarge is its massive memory capacity paired with modest processing power and lower-tier network speeds. While its CPU and memory bandwidth performance are weak, the 244.0 GB RAM allocation makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory density rather than raw compute speed. It is suited for memory-intensive applications, in-memory databases, caching layers, and lightweight text generation tasks where large datasets must reside entirely in RAM.
